components.name: Customer Portal Frontend
components.purpose: Hosts the static and dynamic assets for the customer-facing web application.
components.rationale: Provides fast, secure, and scalable hosting for web applications with built-in CDN capabilities.
trade_offs: Firebase Hosting serves static assets only; server-side rendering would need Cloud Run in front of it.
components.security_considerations: Leverages Firebase's built-in security for content delivery and SSL.

components.name: Backend API
components.purpose: Provides the core business logic and APIs for the customer portal, handling requests from the frontend.
components.rationale: Serverless container platform offers automatic scaling, cost efficiency, and simplified deployment for API services.
trade_offs: Cloud Run scales to zero, so the first request after idle pays a cold start unless minimum instances are kept warm at a cost.
components.security_considerations: Requires proper IAM roles and service accounts, and secure configuration for environment variables.

components.name: Relational Database
components.purpose: Stores customer-specific data, portal configuration, and transactional information.
components.rationale: Managed relational database service provides high availability, backups, and scalability without operational overhead.
trade_offs: Cloud SQL is a single-region managed instance; cross-region high availability needs read replicas and adds cost and replication lag.
components.security_considerations: Requires strong access controls, encryption at rest and in transit, and regular backups.

components.name: Customer Identity Management
components.purpose: Manages customer authentication and authorization for accessing the portal.
components.rationale: A fully managed service for customer identity, supporting various authentication methods and MFA.
trade_offs: Identity Platform is simple to adopt but customising login flows beyond its templates means owning more frontend code.
components.security_considerations: Handles user credentials securely, supports MFA, and integrates with standard identity protocols.

components.name: API Gateway
components.purpose: Provides a unified entry point for external systems and the frontend to interact with the backend services.
components.rationale: Simplifies API management, enforces security policies, and routes requests to appropriate backend services.
trade_offs: API Gateway adds a managed policy layer and a small per-call latency; it has fewer features than Apigee if advanced monetisation is ever needed.
components.security_considerations: Acts as the first line of defense, enforcing authentication, authorization, and rate limiting.

components.name: TMS Integration Connector
components.purpose: Facilitates secure and reliable integration with the existing Transportation Management System (TMS).
components.rationale: Provides managed connectors for various enterprise systems, simplifying data exchange and reducing custom code.
trade_offs: Integration Connectors cut custom code but depend on a supported connector for the TMS; an unsupported system falls back to a custom Cloud Run adapter.
components.security_considerations: Requires secure network connectivity (e.g., Private Service Connect) and credential management.

components.name: Finance System Integration Connector
components.purpose: Facilitates secure and reliable integration with the existing Finance System for invoice retrieval.
components.rationale: Provides managed connectors for various enterprise systems, simplifying data exchange and reducing custom code.
trade_offs: A managed connector limits control over batch windows and retries compared with a custom finance adapter.
components.security_considerations: Requires secure network connectivity (e.g., Private Service Connect) and credential management.

components.name: Payment Gateway Orchestration
components.purpose: Orchestrates the interaction with the external payment gateway for online invoice payments.
components.rationale: Serverless orchestration service allows defining and executing complex sequences of API calls and logic.
trade_offs: Adds a layer of abstraction and potential latency compared to direct integration, but improves reliability and error handling.
components.security_considerations: Handles sensitive payment initiation, requiring secure credential management and error handling.

components.name: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
components.purpose: Provides a logically isolated network environment for all cloud resources, ensuring secure communication.
components.rationale: Essential for network isolation, defining custom IP address ranges, and configuring network policies.
trade_offs: Private networking hardens the platform but every managed service then needs a private access path, which adds setup effort.
components.security_considerations: Forms the foundation of network security, enabling private IP addresses and firewall rules.

components.name: Global Load Balancer
components.purpose: Distributes incoming user traffic across multiple instances of the frontend and backend services for high availability and performance.
components.rationale: Provides global load balancing, SSL termination, and protection against DDoS attacks.
trade_offs: A global load balancer is more than a single-region portal needs today; it is chosen so a second region can be added without re-architecting.
components.security_considerations: Integrates with Cloud Armor for WAF capabilities and DDoS protection.

components.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
components.purpose: Protects the portal from common web vulnerabilities and DDoS attacks.
components.rationale: Provides WAF capabilities and DDoS protection policies integrated with Cloud Load Balancing.
trade_offs: Cloud Armor rules need tuning; strict defaults can block legitimate customer traffic until the rule set is reviewed.
components.security_considerations: Filters malicious traffic before it reaches the application, enhancing overall security posture.

components.name: Secret Manager
components.purpose: Securely stores and manages sensitive information such as API keys, database credentials, and integration secrets.
components.rationale: Centralized secret management service reduces the risk of hardcoding credentials and improves security posture.
trade_offs: Secret Manager is the right store, but services must fetch secrets at start-up, so rotation needs a restart or a refresh routine.
components.security_considerations: Ensures secrets are encrypted at rest and in transit, with fine-grained access control.

components.name: Cloud Logging
components.purpose: Collects and stores logs from all application components and infrastructure services.
components.rationale: Provides a centralized logging solution for debugging, auditing, and security analysis.
trade_offs: Retaining logs for audit increases storage cost; log sinks and exclusions must be designed early.
components.security_considerations: Logs may contain sensitive information and require appropriate access controls and retention policies.

components.name: Cloud Monitoring
components.purpose: Gathers metrics and provides dashboards and alerting for the health and performance of the portal.
components.rationale: Offers comprehensive monitoring capabilities for cloud resources, enabling proactive issue detection.
trade_offs: Useful dashboards and alerts take deliberate work; out of the box the metrics are raw and noisy.
components.security_considerations: Monitoring data should be protected with appropriate IAM roles to prevent unauthorized access.

components.name: Error Reporting
components.purpose: Aggregates and analyzes application errors, providing real-time alerts and insights into error trends.
components.rationale: Automatically identifies and groups application errors, simplifying debugging and incident response.
trade_offs: Error Reporting groups exceptions well for Cloud Run but gives little insight into integration failures outside the service code.
components.security_considerations: Error details might contain sensitive data, requiring careful handling and access restrictions.

components.name: CI/CD Pipeline
components.purpose: Automates the build, test, and packaging of application code into deployable artifacts.
components.rationale: Provides a fully managed CI/CD service that integrates with source repositories and other Google Cloud services.
trade_offs: Cloud Build keeps everything on one platform, but teams already on GitHub Actions or GitLab CI would maintain two pipeline styles.
components.security_considerations: Build processes should run with least privilege and scan for vulnerabilities.

components.name: Deployment Automation
components.purpose: Manages the automated deployment of application artifacts across different environments.
components.rationale: Provides continuous delivery to target environments, managing releases and rollbacks.
trade_offs: Cloud Deploy adds a formal promotion flow, which slows small teams down until the pipeline stages are settled.
components.security_considerations: Deployment pipelines require strict access controls and audit trails.

environments.dev: All components will have dedicated development instances, often with reduced scale or shared resources. Developers will use ARC_16 (Cloud Build) and ARC_17 (Cloud Deploy) for automated deployments to this environment.
environments.test: A dedicated testing environment will mirror production as closely as possible in terms of services and configuration, but with test data. Deployments will be managed by ARC_17 (Cloud Deploy) after successful CI/CD runs.
environments.prod: The production environment will host the live customer portal, configured for high availability, scalability, and security, managed by ARC_17 (Cloud Deploy).

deployment_runtime.text: The customer portal frontend (ARC_01) will be deployed using Firebase Hosting for static content and client-side application. The backend API (ARC_02) will leverage Cloud Run for serverless container deployment, providing automatic scaling and simplified operations. Continuous integration and delivery will be managed by ARC_16 (Cloud Build) for building and testing, and ARC_17 (Cloud Deploy) for orchestrating deployments across environments.

availability_scalability.text: High availability and scalability are achieved through several components. The customer portal frontend (ARC_01) benefits from Firebase Hosting's global CDN. The backend API (ARC_02) on Cloud Run automatically scales based on demand. A Global Load Balancer (ARC_10) distributes traffic, and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (ARC_03) provides a managed, highly available database. Google Cloud Armor (ARC_11) also contributes to availability by mitigating DDoS attacks.

backup_dr.validation_reason: This is a recommended practice not explicitly stated by the customer.
backup_dr.text: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (ARC_03) provides automated backups and point-in-time recovery. Disaster recovery will involve cross-region replication for the database and infrastructure-as-code for rapid re-provisioning of stateless components in a new region.

observability.text: The solution will implement comprehensive observability using Google Cloud services. Cloud Logging (ARC_13) will centralize all application and infrastructure logs. Cloud Monitoring (ARC_14) will provide metrics, dashboards, and alerting for system health and performance. Error Reporting (ARC_15) will automatically detect and group application errors, facilitating rapid debugging and resolution.

security_controls.text: Security is a core consideration, implemented through multiple layers. Customer authentication and authorization are handled by Identity Platform (ARC_04). Network isolation is provided by Virtual Private Cloud (ARC_09). Google Cloud Armor (ARC_11) acts as a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect against common web attacks. Sensitive data like API keys and credentials are securely managed using Secret Manager (ARC_12).
